title: Land Due Diligence Survey in Romania — Verify Before You Buy
metaDescription: Pre-acquisition land due diligence in Romania: land book verification, cadastral overlap detection, real vs deed area measurement, encumbrance reading. For investors, funds and PV developers.
h1: Land Due Diligence Surveys in Romania: Check the Land Before the Money Moves
whatsappPrefillEn: Hello! I need a land due diligence survey in Romania before an acquisition.

sections.heading: Why Romanian land needs technical due diligence, not just legal
sections.html:
Your lawyer checks the contracts. But in Romania, some of the most expensive land problems are technical, invisible in the deeds and visible only to a surveyor with access to the cadastral data:

  • Overlaps: the parcel's registered geometry overlaps a neighbour's — a defect that can freeze any transaction or permit until resolved, and that a paper review will never catch.
  • Real versus deed area: the parcel measures smaller than the documents claim. On a PV site, a few percent of missing area is missing rows of panels; on any purchase, it is money paid for land that does not exist.
  • Position: the land is registered, but not where everyone believes it is — misplaced parcels are a known legacy of how older registrations were made.
  • Encumbrances with physical footprints: easements, protection corridors along power lines or pipelines, and access rights that constrain what can be built where.
  • No registration at all: the "parcel" is an unregistered inheritance share — a different acquisition strategy entirely (see unregistered land).

sections.heading: What the due diligence survey covers
sections.html:
Desk phase (any site in Romania): fresh land book extracts for every parcel, reading of all three sections in plain English, verification of the registered geometry against the national geoportal and cadastral plan, overlap screening, chain-of-title sanity checks, and a written findings report with a clear verdict per parcel: clean / conditional / red flag.

Field phase (Alba, Cluj, Mureș, Sibiu, Hunedoara): control measurements of the actual boundaries and area, verification that occupation on the ground matches the registers, slope and access reality-check, and — for PV acquisitions — the terrain observations that feed buildable-capacity estimates.

For investors buying ready-to-build projects, we additionally re-verify the project's existing survey documentation: coordinate system correctness, OCPI stamps, and whether the drawings match the terrain — errors in inherited documentation surface at the worst possible moment otherwise.

sections.heading: When to commission it
sections.html: Before signing the pre-sale agreement, or at latest before money becomes non-refundable. The survey costs a fraction of any deposit, and its findings become negotiation leverage: a measured shortfall in area or a discovered overlap is either the seller's problem to fix or a price reduction. Our fastest engagements are exactly this — an investor sends land book numbers on WhatsApp, we return the desk verdict within days, and the field verification follows on the parcels that survive it.

items.q: What do you need from us to start?
items.a: Ideally the land book numbers or extracts and the locality; even just the cadastral numbers suffice — the register is public. Send them in the WhatsApp chat and we confirm scope and fee the same day.

items.q: Can you check a site we haven't told the seller we're investigating?
items.a: The desk phase is entirely discreet — land book data is public and consulting it requires no one's consent. Field measurements on private land are arranged with access permission, typically once you are in agreed negotiations.

items.q: How is this different from the notary's checks at signing?
items.a: The notary verifies the legal chain at the moment of sale — ownership, capacity, encumbrances as registered. They do not measure anything, screen geometric overlaps, or verify that reality matches the register. Both checks are necessary; only one involves instruments.

items.q: What does the report look like, and what does it cost?
items.a: A per-parcel findings document in English: register status, geometry verdict, measured versus deed area where field work was done, encumbrances translated and assessed, and a clear recommendation per parcel. The desk phase is a small fixed-scope fee per parcel with portfolio pricing for batches; the field phase is quoted by site. Against the deposit at risk on any serious acquisition, the whole exercise is a rounding error — which is exactly why skipping it is never the economy it appears to be.
